paper_title: ATPlace2.5D: Analytical Thermal-Aware Chiplet Placement Framework for Large-Scale 2.5D-IC

extraction.paper_title: ATPlace2.5D: Analytical Thermal-Aware Chiplet Placement Framework for Large-Scale 2.5D-IC

scenario.figure_or_table: Table 6 (Case 3, thermal-aware optimization), with Table 3 (PDF p.6) and Fig. 5 (PDF p.8)
scenario.description: Benchmark Case 3 of the paper's ten constructed test cases, run with thermal-aware placement. Table 3 gives this case as 8 dies with 8448 nets on a 39.0 x 39.0 mm interposer at 0.6 whitespace. Table 6 reports TAP-2.5D at 94.1 C maximum temperature, 185.20 m total wirelength and 186 min runtime. ATPlace2.5D reaches 92.3 C, 142.42 m and 6 min. The Fig. 5 caption gives a single CPU as 9 x 8 mm and a single DRAM as 9 x 9 mm. The packet gives no per-chiplet coordinates or per-chiplet power for this case.
scenario.architecture: 2.5D-IC with a passive interposer on an organic substrate. Case 3 has 8 chiplets with UCIe x32 advanced-package D2D links. The chiplets are CPU, DRAM and related HPC modules adapted from the TAP-2.5D cases. The primary heat path is TIM, heat spreader and air-forced heatsink, with adiabatic lateral surfaces.
scenario.workload: Worst-case power distribution across chiplets. Power densities in the benchmark range from 2e5 to 3e6 W/m^2. The per-chiplet watt values for Case 3 are not stated in the packet text.
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state temperature at 45 C ambient and a heatsink convective resistance of 0.1 K/W. The heat spreader and heatsink edges are 2x the interposer size. HotSpot 6.0 is the golden simulator on a 64 x 64 grid. The reported thermal observable is the maximum temperature in C (Table 6).

original_setup.solver: Steady-state HotSpot 6.0 on a 64x64 thermal grid is the golden simulator. The optimizer uses a physics-based analytical compact thermal model (approximate Green's function per chiplet, 2N+3 parameters) fitted to HotSpot maps from 5-10 legalized layouts. The model solves the steady-state heat equation with adiabatic lateral boundaries and a primary heat path through TIM, spreader and air-forced heatsink (0.1 K/W, 45 C ambient).
original_setup.optimizer: ATPlace2.5D. MILP initialization (Gurobi), then orientation-aware analytical placement by Polak-Ribiere conjugate gradient descent on wirelength + lambda_therm*R[T] + lambda_dens*density penalty, then MILP legalization (Gurobi). Hyperparameters are tuned by Optuna Bayesian optimization.
original_setup.controller: None. This is a static design-time chiplet placement with no runtime thermal controller.
original_setup.benchmark: Case 3 of the paper's ten constructed benchmark cases (8 dies, 8448 nets, x32 UCIe bump type, 39.0 x 39.0 mm interposer, 0.6 whitespace), run as thermal-aware optimization and compared with SA-based TAP-2.5D (Table 3 PDF p.6, Table 6 PDF p.7).

thermal_observable.location: Maximum temperature of the final ATPlace2.5D thermal-aware placement for Case 3 (Table 6, Tmax column). The paper does not state the layer explicitly; the temperature map is on the 64x64 thermal grid of the HotSpot-validated model.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum (Tmax) over the steady-state temperature map under the worst-case power distribution; a single scalar per placement.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper models a 2.5D-IC with a passive interposer (RDL, TSVs, microbumps, C4 pillars, organic substrate) and heterogeneous epoxy-filled layers. A simple 2D steady-state Studio model cannot represent these layers, so the layer stack and bump/TSV effective conductivities are not reproduced.

The cooling model is an air-forced heatsink with a 0.1 K/W convective resistance. The spreader and heatsink edges are 2x the interposer, ambient is 45 C, lateral surfaces are adiabatic, and the secondary path through substrate and PCB is ignored. Studio cooling and boundary conditions may differ, which shifts absolute temperatures.

The solver differs. The published values come from HotSpot 6.0 (64x64 grid) and an analytical compact model with MAE of about 1.2 C, whereas Studio uses its own solver. The reported 92.3 C cannot be matched exactly.

The paper's objective is a placement optimizer with MILP initialization, CGD, legalization and Bayesian hyperparameter tuning, balancing wirelength and temperature. Studio can at most evaluate a given fixed floorplan and does not reproduce the optimizer or the wirelength results.
The paper is steady-state only, with no transient behaviour, runtime controller or reliability analysis, so there is no transient or controller mismatch beyond the absence of these features.

methods.note: The paper's methods are text-verified: HotSpot 6.0 on a 64x64 grid, a 2N+3-parameter compact Green's-function model, MILP init, Polak-Ribiere CGD, and MILP legalization. But the extraction marks the scenario steady_2d_relevant=true and sets experiment.kind=custom_2d_steady. It also lists as essential mismatches the multilayer 2.5D stack (substrate, C4, TSV, interposer, microbump, epoxy), the heatsink path and the different solver. Those mismatches contradict the 2D claim. The paper's thermal model is a layered 3D-style stack, so this cannot be called a 2D reproduction.

code.note: The packet has no assets and no repository link. The ATPlace2.5D code is not linked, and the TAP-2.5D open-source code is mentioned without a URL. The HotSpot configuration files are not available either. Nothing in the packet can verify the implementation.

parameters.note: Scalar values are text-supported: 45 C ambient, 0.1 K/W, 100 um gap, 64x64 grid, 8 dies, 8448 nets, 39x39 mm interposer, and Tmax 92.3/94.1 C. Decisive parameters are missing: per-chiplet power in W for Case 3 (only a benchmark-wide 2e5-3e6 W/m^2 range is given), per-chiplet sizes (only a single CPU of 9x8 mm and a single DRAM of 9x9 mm are given from the Fig. 5 caption), chiplet counts by type, layer thicknesses, material properties, and TIM/spreader/heatsink dimensions. The lambda values, lr_pos/lr_ang, epsilon, and the Optuna-tuned hyperparameters are also not stated. The whitespace '0.6' is labeled '%' in the table header, but the 0.35-0.65 range indicates a fraction, so the unit is ambiguous.

config.note: The experiment has an empty floorplan and an empty power_w. No block names, same-scenario coordinates or per-block watts exist, so no floorplan block has same-scenario power. The Case 3 final layout exists only graphically in Fig. 5, and no text evidence shows it was visually checked or digitized. Studio package and material assumptions are absent. The boundary conditions (adiabatic lateral surfaces, spreader and heatsink edges at 2x the interposer) cannot be mapped to a concrete configuration. The 2x factor wording is ambiguous.

assessment.summary: The selected scenario is Case 3 of ATPlace2.5D (8 chiplets, 8448 nets, 39 x 39 mm interposer, thermal-aware placement). The paper reports Tmax of 92.3 C for ATPlace2.5D and 94.1 C for TAP-2.5D, with HotSpot 6.0 on a 64x64 grid as the steady-state golden simulator. The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only, but the deterministic gate failed on input validity (no floorplan blocks and no power_w object), so simulation_allowed is false and the Studio run was skipped. The experiment kind was custom_2d_steady. Even if it had run, it would have produced a steady 2D result with no transient trace. No Studio temperature exists, so no numerical comparison with 92.3 C is made and comparison_valid is false. Nothing here is a replication, exact or approximate. The only defensible conclusion is qualitative. The paper is a steady-state, design-time placement study in which temperature depends on chiplet placement, spacing and power density. This could in principle be probed with a fixed floorplan in a 2D steady model, but the inputs needed for that are not available. The final verdict is therefore not a validated reproduction. It is a gated, skipped illustrative case, with several evidence items also failing the page/asset locator checks and adversarial and independent reviews unresolved.
limitations: Studio did not run: the custom experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w, so no simulated temperature exists and no comparison to the paper's 92.3 C or 94.1 C can be made.

Per-chiplet coordinates, sizes and watts for Case 3 are not available. Only a CPU of 9 x 8 mm and a DRAM of 9 x 9 mm are given as single-instance caption dimensions, and the benchmark-wide power density range is 2e5 to 3e6 W/m^2. Case 3 chiplet counts and types are unspecified, and no total power is stated.

Essential physical mismatches: the paper's multilayer 2.5D stack (passive interposer, RDL, TSVs, microbumps, C4, substrate, epoxy fill) cannot be represented in a simple 2D steady model. The paper's cooling (0.1 K/W air-forced heatsink, 45 C ambient, spreader/heatsink at 2x interposer edge, adiabatic lateral surfaces) may not match Studio boundary conditions, and the solver differs (HotSpot 6.0 64x64 plus a compact model with about 1.25 C MAE on Case 3).

The reported Tmax is a maximum over a temperature map with unstated layer and exact location. Even a matching Studio maximum would not be directly comparable unless layer, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions were shown to match.
The optimizer (MILP, conjugate gradient descent, legalization, Bayesian tuning) and the wirelength and runtime results cannot be reproduced by Studio, which could at most evaluate a fixed floorplan.

Many evidence items lack valid page or pinned asset locators, no paper thermal observable or regime was accepted by the gate, adversarial checks (methods, code, parameters, config, data) are unresolved, and independent verification is pending. No linked code, data or Studio package assumptions exist.
The whitespace unit (percent vs fraction) is ambiguous, and the spreader/heatsink edge-ratio wording is ambiguous.
